newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Thirty Indonesian riot suspects sent to court.
newsitem.headline: Thirty Indonesian riot suspects sent to court.

text.p: Indonesian police apparently have sped up the trial process for 30 people suspected of involvement in a riot last week in central Java that targeted ethnic Chinese, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Monday.

The riot was on Wednesday, and the trial of 12 suspects began on the next day. Eighteen others were brought to court on Saturday, it quoted Pekalongan police chief Lieutenant-Colonel Triyono as saying.
Triyono did not say what charges the suspects faced, but the Post quoted another policeman as saying those in the first group were charged with damaging property and disrupting public order.
Indonesian criminal cases usually take months to process.

At least 60 shops were burned or ransacked, two cars were set ablaze and a state-run bank was damaged during Wednesday's violence, in which about 1,000 people attacked the property of mainly ethnic Chinese.

Eight people were injured during the riot, apparently sparked by reports that a popular singer who used to be a supporter of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) had switched allegiance to the ruling Golkar party.
Some reports said people were angered when Golkar workers took down PPP flags before a planned Golkar rally in the town.
Pekalongan was the only city in central Java that Golkar lost to the PPP in the 1992 general elections.
The next general elections will be on May 29. Under Indonesian law, the only parties allowed to contest the poll are Golkar, PPP and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
Pekalongan's riot was the first in Java since January, when a mob attacked Chinese homes and businesses, Christian churches and Buddhist temples in Renasdengklok in West Java province.
